THE FIRST FIVE MINUTES

Chess is a conversation.

You and your opponent take turns moving one piece. Your goal is checkmate: attack their king so it has no legal escape.

  1. Choose a white piece. Dots show legal destinations.
  2. Choose a destination. Read the coach’s preview, then play the move.
  3. Keep your king safe. “Check” means it is under attack and you must respond.
  4. Experiment freely. Use a hint or take back your last turn.

Castling, promotion, en passant and draw rules are handled for you. Start with Learn step by step to meet each piece.

Play from your keyboard

B focuses the board. Use arrow keys to find a piece, then Enter to select it. Navigate to its destination and press Enter for a preview; press Enter again to play.

H hint · U undo · M movement map · N next exercise when complete · Esc cancel · ? this guide.

You can also type moves such as e2e4, Nf3, or O-O below the board. Shortcuts stay out of the way while you type or use a menu.

Keyboard: arrows move between squares. Enter inspects a square; Enter again tries a legal move. Escape closes the explorer. Tab reaches the piece and promotion menus.

This maps one piece’s options in one position. Try a move to explore the next position. On an open board, maps show movement patterns without king-safety restrictions.
